RFC9552-5.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c22 judge): stale only because TestNoDescriptorEmitsADescendingTLVSequence lost its SRv6SIDs fixture line with the D-8 field deletion; every other descriptor and assertion kept, revert record on addressTLVs re-observed red. Finding of 2026-09-30 unchanged: TestRFC9552NativeLinkTLVsCanonicalOrder and TestRFC9552NativeLinkTLVsReorderedSource drive ls_export encodeNativeLink and assert the exact canonical sequence from an ascending and an interleaved descending source.

RFC9552-5.1-2.note: rejudge 2026-09-30 (was wrong: the units asserted repeated 518 inside a Node Descriptor, which 5.2.1.4 forbids; those tags are removed under D-15 and the units kept untagged). Now proven on the one producer that repeats a Type: the two ls_export units emit two 259, two 260, two 261, two 262 and assert them ascending by Value, and that no longer same-type TLV precedes a shorter one. The Length key never differs within a Type on this producer (259/260 are 4 octets, 261/262 16), so the Length clause is met by construction and asserted as a tie; the Value clause is discriminated: judge break (Value comparison reversed) turns both units red, revert records observed red.

RFC9552-5.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c24 judge). Both halves are now proven on the propagation rail: TestRFC9552UnknownTypesPropagateOnAForwardedUpdate drives forwardUpdateCore to an internal peer and asserts the Node NLRI (unassigned sub-TLV 700) after the MP_REACH next hop and the BGP-LS Attribute value (unassigned TLV 65000, unexpected Link TLV 1088) leave byte-identical. The negative is an R1(b) genuine negative: TestRFC9552UnknownTypesSurviveARewrittenUpdate forces a re-encode toward an external peer (AS_PATH asserted re-encoded with 65000 prepended) and asserts both halves still byte-identical. Judge overlay probe (attrEmitter.keep flipping the last octet of a kept MP_REACH_NLRI) turned both units red on the NLRI assertion; the author's probe (attrEmitter.keep dropping attribute 29) turned both red on the attribute. The HEAD framing-refusal negative was moved to RFC9552-8.2.2-10 under R1 (D-15). TestRFC7752UnknownTLVPreservedAndPropagated (ls) stays as the decoder-level positive.

RFC9552-5.1-4.note: c23 rejudge: only the comment of ls.TestRFC9552AttributeSyntaxStillRejected changed (it now names its decodeAttrTLV assertion as the Consumer decoder check, which matches the body); this row's negative claim there (an unknown TLV is tolerated only while its declared length fits) is the iterateAttrTLVs/decodeAllAttrTLVs ErrBGPLSTruncated assertion, unchanged. Receive-path NLRI units with records on bgplsNLRIWellFormed (c21) unchanged; c23 adds TLV 65000 tolerated by validateBGPLSAttr on the session path (TestRFC9552BGPLSAttributeSemanticErrorsAreNotMalformed, tagged 8.2.2-2/-3)

RFC9552-5.1-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c21 judge). Section 5.1's three ordering clauses are now all driven through enforceRFC7606: type (existing descending 257-before-256 unit), same-type Length (TLV 1234 lengths 3 then 2 discarded; 2 then 3 kept byte-identical) and same-type Value (equal lengths, bb bb then aa aa discarded; aa aa then bb bb kept). Each malformed case is otherwise well framed, so only the order trips, and the survivor beside it is kept. Records observed red on bgplsTLVOrdered.

RFC9552-5.2-6.note: c23: add and remove now driven (TestRFC9552NativeDescriptorTLVAddRemoveWithdrawsFirst: TLV 260 added then removed, each time a del of exactly the previous NLRI precedes the add) beside the HEAD modify +/-; wire half TestRFC9552LinkStateWithdrawalLeavesInMPUnreach pins MP_UNREACH_NLRI = 40 04 47 + exact NLRI with empty Withdrawn Routes and NLRI. Records: revert on reconcilePeer and buildBatchWithdrawUpdate. Judge probes: skipping the withdraw when a replacement exists turned the add/remove unit red; routing AFI 16388 into Withdrawn Routes turned the wire unit red. The update-handler hop between them is generic and untagged. Sub-TLV changes alter the containing TLV value, the modify case

RFC9552-5.2-7.note: c23: send side driven through AnnounceNLRIBatch: + a peer with (16388,71) negotiated gets one UPDATE whose MP_REACH_NLRI starts 40 04 47; - an IPv4-only peer gets no UPDATE and ErrNoPeersAcceptedFamily. Records: revert on AnnounceNLRIBatch both polarities, Negotiate for the capability negative (prose narrowed to what Negotiate asserts, matching its body). Judge targeted probe: removing nc.Has(batch.Family) from the family gate turned the negative red and left the positive green, so the gate itself is what the negative proves. Receive side (an unnegotiated peer sending Link-State NLRI) not driven; the HEAD advertise/negotiate positive in capability holds no record

RFC9552-5.2.1-1.note: c23 rejudge: the IS-IS producer is now proven for both types (TestRFC9552ISISNodeCarriesBothRouterIDs: TLV 134 -> 1028 and TLV 140 -> 1029 with their values, revert record on isis lsp). Still weak: the OSPF producer (ospf/bgpls_export.go adds 1028/1029 from the TE Router Address) has no tagged unit, queued while the ospf package is held (R6), and no unit follows the node attribute onto the BGP-LS Attribute wire

RFC9552-5.2.1.1-1.note: First judgement 2026-10-02 (BGP c22 judge). Positive TestSameNodeHasOneKeyWhateverTheStorageOrder parses one node from two wire orders (512,514,515 and 515,514,512) and asserts both re-encode to the identical canonical bytes, equal to the ascending order: an order-dependent parse or encode goes red (revert record on parseNodeDescriptorTLVsAt observed red). Negative TestNodeDescriptorWriteToMatchesBytes asserts WriteTo and Bytes emit identical octets for one node, so the encoder choice cannot give a second key; it carries no record because Bytes/WriteTo repeat in types_descriptor.go and cannot be producer keys (journal row 2026-10-02).

RFC9552-5.2.1.4-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c22 judge). D-8 fixed at the producer: NodeDescriptor.SRv6SIDs deleted, every Node Descriptor field single-valued and written at most once by NodeDescriptor.WriteTo; TLV 518 is read by parseSRv6SIDDescriptorTLVs into the SRv6 SID NLRI's own SRv6 SID Descriptor, where RFC 9514 Section 6 places it ('This field MUST contain a single SRv6 SID Information TLV'). Sender half: positive TestNodeDescriptorNeverRepeatsASubTLVType sets every field and asserts 512..517 each exactly once and six types; negative TestSRv6SIDNLRIKeepsItsSIDOutOfTheNodeDescriptor encodes an SRv6 SID NLRI with a SID and asserts no type repeats inside the Local Node Descriptors container, no 518 there, one 518 at NLRI level. Judge overlay probe (WriteTo writing TLV 512 twice) turned BOTH units red naming 'sub-TLV type 512 written 2 times'. Receive half unchanged from c21 (duplicate 512 NLRI discarded, distinct types kept). Records: revert on types.go::writeTLV (positive) and types.go::WriteTLVBytes (negative) observed red; they prove reach, because NodeDescriptor.WriteTo cannot be a producer key (three WriteTo in the file, journal row 2026-10-02 gate-excludes-part-of-its-population) and gomu mutants inside it (report run 2026-10-02) are refused for the same reason. The receive units carry no record (pre-existing).

RFC9552-5.2.1.4-2.note: single-polarity positive per row annotation; asserts the exact ascending sub-TLV sequence 512..517 from NodeDescriptor.WriteTo

RFC9552-5.2.2-1.note: c23: genuine negative under R1(b): TestRFC9552NativeDualStackLinkKeepsEveryAddress forces link ids 7/9 and IPv4+IPv6 globals on both ends and asserts TLVs 259, 260, 261, 262 each exactly once with their values (revert record on encodeNativeLink). Judge probe dropping the IPv6 interface address when IPv4 is present turned it red on TLV 261. HEAD positive TestRFC9552NativeLinkIdentitySelection pins exact values; HEAD invalid-zero-address negative stays as a supplement

RFC9552-5.2.2-2.note: negative asserts TLV 258 absent from a link carrying global addresses and link IDs; positive asserts the link is still advertised by 261/260

RFC9552-5.2.2-3.note: negative asserts link-local 169.254/fe80 addresses absent from 259-262 (exact single global values), and a link-local-only link carries none of 259-262; positive pins the global addresses once each

RFC9552-5.2.2-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c22 judge). First clause now driven: TestRFC9552NativeUnnumberedLinkCarriesLinkIdentifiers exports an IS-IS link with no interface or neighbor address and link ids 7/9 and asserts TLV 258 == 00000007 00000009 and none of 259-262. Second clause (link-local-only addressing) stays on TestRFC9552NativeLinkIdentitySelection. Row carries {single-polarity: positive}, read against encodeNativeLink: no refusal input exists. Revert records on encodeNativeLink observed red for both units.

RFC9552-5.2.2-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c22 judge). Genuine negative added: TestRFC9552NativeLinkNonDefaultTopologyNotCollapsed feeds one IS-IS link in topologies 0, 2, 2 and asserts exactly two Link NLRIs, each with exactly one TLV 263, MT-IDs {0,2}: a producer collapsing onto the default topology or dropping 263 on the topology-2 NLRI goes red. Positive TestRFC9552NativeLinkNonDefaultTopology asserts 263 = MT-ID 2; its inline negative tag still re-asserts the same value and proves nothing on its own. Over-constraint noted: the negative also requires TLV 263 with MT-ID 0 on the default-topology NLRI, which RFC 9552 does not require (only the non-default case is a MUST). Revert records on encodeNativeLink observed red.

RFC9552-8.2.2-1.note: c23: session path driven through enforceRFC7606 (reactor rfc9552_semantic_test.go). + three NLRIs wrong only in content (Protocol-ID 200 with empty TLV 256; 2-octet AS sub-TLV; Link NLRI without TLV 257) kept byte-identical beside a survivor; - each framing twin (one length octet past its container) discarded, survivor kept. Revert records on bgplsNLRIWellFormed both polarities. Judge overlay probes: adding each semantic check (Protocol-ID range, AS sub-TLV length 4, TLV 257 required) turned the matching positive subtest red with the twins green; a no-walk probe (return true) turned every twin red. HEAD decoder-level units in nlri/ls rfc9552_test.go stay as supplementary and hold no records

RFC9552-8.2.2-10.note: Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c24 judge) after the ls tag move. Reactor positives drive a TLV overrunning the attribute and a trailing half-header (both sum-to-length failures) to Attribute Discard with a tombstone; the negative keeps a well-formed attribute byte-identical. Added positive ls.TestRFC7752MalformedTLVNotPreserved: the ls decoder's walk (iterateAttrTLVs, decodeAllAttrTLVs) refuses an overrunning TLV with ErrBGPLSTruncated and AttrTLVsToJSON yields nothing; recorded red on iterateAttrTLVs. The recognized sub-TLV clause stays vacuous on the session path because ze recognizes no BGP-LS Attribute TLV there (rfc7606_bgpls.go).

RFC9552-8.2.2-2.note: c23: session path driven through enforceRFC7606. + four attributes wrong only in content (descending order, TLV 1024 twice, 3-octet TLV 1088 beside a Node NLRI, TLV 65000 with reserved flag bits): action None and the attribute byte-identical; - each twin whose last TLV declares 16 octets: Attribute Discard, attribute gone. Revert records on validateBGPLSAttr. Judge probes: a semantic check in validateBGPLSAttr (order, repeat, unregistered type, 1088 length) turned each positive subtest red; return-nil turned each twin red. The HEAD negative ls.TestRFC9552AttributeSyntaxStillRejected comment now names its decodeAttrTLV assertion as the Consumer's decoder check, matching the body; that unit holds no record

RFC9552-8.2.2-3.note: c23: the Propagator receive path (enforceRFC7606, reactor binary links the ls plugin so the Consumer decoders coexist) refuses none of the three semantic NLRIs nor the four semantic attributes, and still discards every framing twin; +/- revert records on bgplsNLRIWellFormed and validateBGPLSAttr. The same judge probes as 8.2.2-1/-2 show the positives fail on any added semantic check and the negatives on a dropped syntactic walk. HEAD decoder-level tags remain unrecorded supplements

RFC9552-8.2.2-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c21 judge): stale only because TestRFC9552LinkStateNLRIWithUnknownTLVsIsPropagated gained a 5.1-4 tag line; its body is unchanged. RFC9552-8.2.2-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c21 judge): stale only because TestRFC9552LinkStateNLRIWithUnknownTLVsIsPropagated gained a 5.1-4 tag line; its body is unchanged. Total NLRI Length overrunning MP_REACH gives RFC7606ActionSessionReset; a well-formed section leaves the session up.

RFC9552-8.2.2-6.note: TLV overrun and trailing-octet attributes give AttributeDiscard with tombstone and MP_REACH kept; a well-formed attribute survives byte-identically

RFC9552-8.2.2-9.note: Re-judged 2026-10-01 (BGP c21 judge). The two bullets the earlier note named are now driven through enforceRFC7606: MP_UNREACH_NLRI length sum (Total NLRI Length 255 with 21 present: session reset + error, TestRFC9552LinkStateUnreachLengthOverrunResetsSession) and the sub-TLV length of a recognized TLV (TLV 256 framed at 8, sub-TLV 512 claiming 8 with 4 present: NLRI discarded, survivor kept). With the existing MP_REACH sum, TLV overrun, ordering and duplicate sub-TLV units and the well-formed negative, every concrete bullet of the section 8.2.2 list is driven; the 'per RFC 7606' bullet is the umbrella of the others. New units carry records observed red on validateBGPLSNLRISyntax and bgplsNodeDescriptorWellFormed; older units carry none (pre-existing).
